clue.text: Be lustful in iron spire

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the lustful word sits inside the symbol for iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
to lech is to behave lustfully

explanation.surface: Someone is told to feel desire inside an iron church spire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be lustful' looks like the definition, but it is wordplay; the definition is 'spire', which sits over the crossing of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A flèche is a slender spire, typically rising from where nave and transepts cross in a church.

clue.text: Boy brought up to property right

indicators.note: in a down light, bringing a word up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: Neil is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad is raised with an eye to his property rights.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to keep another's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Detectives stamped around and met one another

indicators.note: 'around' puts the stamped word round the detectives

parts.note: coined, as metal is stamped into coins
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Police officers stamped about the place and eventually ran into each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that coincided happened together or met at the same point in time or space.

clue.text: They walk out of the next European Union assembly

indicators.note: an assembly puts parts together in a new arrangement, so these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A stage direction for delegates leaving the next session of a European Union gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' reads as a parliament but is the anagram signal on NEXT plus EU. The answer is Latin stage direction for several actors leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is the Latin stage direction meaning that several characters leave the stage.

clue.text: A villain's leavings, perhaps

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says these letters might form something else, an invitation to rearrange them

explanation.surface: What a scoundrel leaves behind might be his scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the villain is, perhaps, a rearranged 'leavings'. Svengali is the sinister hypnotist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali, the manipulative hypnotist of the novel Trilby, has become a byword for a sinister controlling figure.

clue.text: Very British memsahib, half drunk, gives vent to salty oath

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, so the letters are jumbled
half of memsahib means its first four letters only

explanation.surface: A tipsy colonial memsahib, very British, lets fly with a sailor's curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges VERY, BRITISH and MEMS (the first half of memsahib). 'gives vent to' is linking. A memsahib was a European married woman in colonial India.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is the stock oath of a stage pirate or old sea dog, salty meaning nautical.

clue.text: Service boy in retribution, topped and tailed

indicators.note: 'in' puts the boy inside the trimmed word
the word loses its first and last letters, as a vegetable loses its ends

parts.note: revenge is retribution
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A church service where a boy is caught up in vengeance with something trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped and tailed' drops the first and last letters of the retribution word; the boy then goes into the middle of what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening church service of the Anglican church.

clue.text: Reptile shooting coke by the gram

indicators.note: shooting suggests something fired off and scattered, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A lizard caught taking cocaine by the gram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' reads as injecting drugs but signals the anagram of COKE; 'by the' just links it to G.
explanation.definitionFit: A gecko is a small lizard, and lizards are reptiles: an example of the class.

clue.text: County in real trouble accepting money

indicators.note: 'accepting' means the jumbled letters take the money inside them
in trouble the letters are put in disarray

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: A county in genuine financial difficulty taking in funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges IN REAL into LANIRE, which is split by CASH. Lancashire is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is a county of north-west England, an example of the category.

clue.text: Live right by peninsula, almost in disorder

parts.note: to be is to live, to exist

indicators.note: almost means the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula of Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: Living on the right side of Spain, nearly in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' looks like an anagram signal after 'in', but it is the definition: a medical disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a disease caused by vitamin B1 deficiency, a medical disorder.

clue.text: Even Seb retires in old age

indicators.note: 'retires' means the words go backwards, as one retreating

parts.note: ene is an old Scots form of even, meaning evening
Seb Coe is the British Olympic middle-distance runner

explanation.surface: Even the athlete Seb is retiring in his twilight years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retires' turns the whole run ENE COE backwards. 'age' here is a geological period.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eocene is an epoch of geological time some 56 to 34 million years ago, an ancient period.

clue.text: Where to admit fuel muffling neo-Nazis' noises off

indicators.note: muffling means wrapping up, so the fuel wraps round the rest

parts.note: coal is a fuel
the NF, National Front, was a far-right British party

indicators.note: off means not right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fuel muffles the noises of extremists somewhere offstage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the noises; 'muffling' wraps the fuel round them and the neo-Nazis. 'Where to admit' means where one admits sins.
explanation.definitionFit: A confessional is the booth in a church where penitents admit their sins to a priest.

clue.text: Notice silver in a lot of make-up on the island

indicators.note: 'in' places notice and silver inside the shortened make-up
a lot of a word is most of it, here all but its last letter

parts.note: mascara is eye make-up
an ad, or advertisement, is a notice
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An advert in silver appears in a pile of cosmetics on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims MASCARA to MASCAR; ADAG goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascar is the large island nation off the south-east coast of Africa.

clue.text: Wicked woman interrupting strumpet

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the woman sits inside

parts.note: bad means wicked

explanation.surface: A wicked woman barges in on a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked woman' looks like the definition, but it is the two pieces; the definition is 'strumpet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bawd and a strumpet are both old words for a woman of loose morals.

clue.text: Compiler's carrying on with affected type of government

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so these go inside

parts.note: the setter, the compiler, would say my
taken as written
arch means affectedly knowing or playful

explanation.surface: The setter is carrying on with a pretentious political system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying on' looks like one phrase, but 'carrying' is the container signal and 'on' is a piece taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchy is rule by a king or queen, a kind of state government.

clue.text: Concerning each politician and what one can perform

parts.note: re means concerning, about
per means each, as in per head
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A remark about every politician and their range of party tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A repertory, or repertoire, is the stock of pieces a performer or company is ready to play.

clue.text: Swan to make off with Molly Bloom's original

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
to elope is to run off secretly

explanation.surface: A swan runs away, taking a character from Joyce's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Molly Bloom, wife of Leopold in Joyce's Ulysses, is modelled on Penelope, wife of Odysseus.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce built Ulysses on the Odyssey, so Odysseus's faithful wife is the model for Molly Bloom.

clue.text: Toughest stag gives up the ghost inside

indicators.note: 'inside' puts the dying inside the stag

parts.note: a hart is a male deer, a stag
dies, as an idiom

explanation.surface: Even the toughest stag eventually expires within.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardiest is the superlative of hardy, meaning toughest or most robust.

clue.text: Leave a bit

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for departing and a noun for a portion of a whole.

clue.text: Amusing scene involving a basket chair

indicators.note: 'involving' says the words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A comic scene centred on a wicker chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a short comic scene in a revue or comedy show.

clue.text: A political craftsman?

parts.note: read politically, one who forms a government's top ministers; literally, a joiner who builds fine furniture

explanation.definitionFit: A cabinetmaker is a skilled woodworker who makes fine furniture such as cupboards.

clue.text: Grandma entered? That's fatuous!

indicators.note: entered means went into, so grandma goes inside

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is
nan is an informal word for grandma

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the news that grandma has come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' looks like part of an exclamation, but it is IE, which Grandma enters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or pointless, a close synonym of fatuous.

clue.text: What to bend after a monarch is born?

indicators.note: 'after' places the born word following the monarch

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king
née means born, used of a maiden name

explanation.surface: A question about bowing when a new king arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a cryptic definition, but there is wordplay: K then NEE.
explanation.definitionFit: One bends the knee in deference before a monarch, so it is the thing that bends.

clue.text: Book size for old firm to put tax returns in

indicators.note: 'to put ... in' says the reversed tax goes inside the firm

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: An old company files its tax returns in a particular format of book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax returns' reads as forms filed with the taxman, but 'returns' is the reversal signal on the tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavo is a book size made by folding a sheet into eight leaves.

clue.text: Newt with young inhaling oxygen at once, once

parts.note: an eft is a newt

indicators.note: inhaling means taking in, so oxygen goes inside

parts.note: sons are young, offspring
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A newt and its offspring breathe in oxygen immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'once' tells us the word is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Eftsoons is an archaic adverb meaning soon afterwards or forthwith.

clue.text: Wessex girl clutching cylinder, missing the greenwood

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so Tess wraps round the cylinder

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Hardy's heroine from Wessex
a reel is a cylinder for winding thread or film

explanation.surface: Hardy's Tess grips a spool while far from the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Wessex is Thomas Hardy's fictional name for south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Treeless means without trees, so missing the greenwood, a poetic word for forest.

clue.text: Tough little lady's alter ego admitting nothing new

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so nothing goes inside

parts.note: Mr Hyde is Dr Jekyll's alter ego
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A tomboy's other self lets in nothing new.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has'. 'alter ego' needs Stevenson's Jekyll and Hyde.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoyden is a boisterous, tomboyish girl, a tough little lady.
